faq.platforms.a: No. Each platform is a separate purchase from its own store: the App Store for iPhone and iPad, the Mac App Store for Mac and the Microsoft Store for Windows. Buying on iPhone and iPad does not include Mac or Windows, and buying on a computer does not include iPhone and iPad.
faq.restore.a: With your 24 recovery words. Backups of your iPhone, iPad or Mac do not include your identity, so restoring a device backup does not bring it back. Install Doughnut Forge on the new device, choose “I already have recovery words” and enter them. It works across platforms, for example from a Mac to a Windows PC. Restoring brings back your identity, so files encrypted for it open again. Your recovery words do not bring back your contacts. If you first restore a backup of your iPhone, iPad or Mac and then enter your recovery words, your contacts come back too.
faq.data.a: The app collects nothing: it has no tracking, analytics or crash reporting. This website keeps only anonymous daily totals of page views, which anyone can see on its statistics page. The count sets no cookies and never keeps your IP address. The only things this website stores on your device are your choice not to be counted, if you make it, and one build number, so an open tab can tell when the site has been updated. Apple and Microsoft may share aggregated statistics, such as download counts, that contain no personal details. GitHub, which hosts this website, may log technical information such as your IP address. The privacy policy has the details.

faq.share.a: Ask the other person for their contact card (a .vltc2 file) and add it to your Contacts. Then encrypt the file and choose them as someone who can open it. Send the encrypted file any way you like, such as by email, in a messaging app or on a USB stick. Only the people you chose can open it.
technical.visible.older: Files made with versions older than 0.4.41 show who they are for, and who sent them, without the key. They still open in the current version.
security.quantum.title: Post-quantum encryption
security.quantum.text: Doughnut Forge is designed to resist attacks by future quantum computers, using NIST-standardised post-quantum algorithms alongside classical ones.
faq.quantum.a: In the future, powerful quantum computers may be able to break some of the encryption that is widely used today. Doughnut Forge is designed to resist attacks by future quantum computers, using NIST-standardised post-quantum algorithms alongside classical ones.
meta.technical.description: The standard methods Doughnut Forge uses: AES-256-GCM, X25519 with ML-KEM-768, Argon2id, what can be seen without the key, and its network behaviour.
technical.keys.exchange.text: each item's key is sealed separately for every recipient, and for you, using X25519 together with ML-KEM-768. The two shared secrets are combined with SHA-256.
technical.keys.signatures.text: Ed25519, used to sign contact cards. Proof of who sent an item is not yet offered.
technical.stored.text: Your secret is stored only in encrypted form. It is encrypted with AES-256-GCM, using a key made from your password with Argon2id:
technical.visible.count.text: visible (the number of recipients, counting the sender).
technical.limits.sender.label: Proof of who sent an item.
technical.limits.sender.text: Doughnut Forge does not yet prove who sent an item.
technical.limits.visible.label: Size, number of recipients and file name.
